sources.entry: Zipline - A lightweight, fast and reliable file sharing server that is commonly used with ShareX, offering a react-based Web UI and fast API. MIT Docker/Nodejs
Zipline | ShareX and file upload server with URL shortening

summary.one_liner: Zipline is a self-hostable file upload and sharing server, the "next generation ShareX / file upload server," with a web UI, API, and URL shortening.
summary.what_it_does: Zipline runs as a server that accepts uploads of any file type and stores them on the local filesystem or in S3-compatible storage. It provides folders, tags, URL shortening, embeds, and password protection for shared files. Users can sign in with OAuth2, 2FA, or passkeys, and admins can set invites and quotas. It includes image compression, video thumbnails, Discord and HTTP webhooks, custom themes, and a PWA. The README describes it as working with ShareX and having an API. Installation is documented primarily through a Docker Compose setup with PostgreSQL.
use_cases: Sharing files and images via short links
Hosting a private image or file host for a team
Managing uploads with per-user quotas and invites
Embedding shared media with link previews
how_to_run: Create a .env file with POSTGRESQL_PASSWORD and CORE_SECRET (see the Generating Secrets section of the README)
Create a docker-compose.yml with postgres:16 and ghcr.io/diced/zipline services as shown in the README
Open the site on port 3000 (or the port set by CORE_PORT)
notable: Built for ShareX with an API and web UI
Supports local storage or S3 as the storage backend
Has a built-in importer for migrating data from Zipline v3
caveats: Requires a CPU with AVX support; no binaries or images for non-AVX CPUs
No upgrade path from v3 to v4; data must be exported and imported
Requires PostgreSQL and a CORE_SECRET to start
